parsed.rationale: Both `ProcessInfo.ThermalState.description` (in the sample-app `DebugHUD.swift` at line 237) and `PerformanceControls.thermalStateLabel` (in the production `PerformanceControls.swift` at line 152) are computed properties in the same `Wallpaper` package that almost certainly map a `ProcessInfo.ThermalState` value to a human-readable string, evidenced by a Jaccard similarity of 0.75. Because one record is `is_sample_app: true` and the other is production code, the duplication is not purely intentional — the sample app is mirroring logic that already exists (or should exist) in the main library. The cleanest fix is to add a single `extension ProcessInfo.ThermalState` with a `description` (or `displayLabel`) computed property inside the `Wallpaper` package's shared sources (e.g., a new file `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Extensions/ThermalState+Description.swift`), then have both call sites reference that single implementation.
